title: Exploring the psychology of LLMs' Moral and Legal Reasoning

bias_targets.methodology: Administering the Moral Foundations Questionnaire (MFQ) and a political ideology self-identification scale to evaluate models' alignment with liberal, conservative, or moderate orientations.

Using vignette-based experiments (both between-subjects and within-subjects) to measure how knowledge of a bad versus neutral outcome alters the models' ex-post judgments of probability, negligence, blame, and punishment.

Replicating psychological experiments (such as the Knobe effect and abnormal selection in causation) to test if the moral valence of an action (e.g., helping vs. harming, or norm-conforming vs. norm-violating) systematically skews the models' ascriptions of intentionality, rule violation, and causality.
